An Eastern Orthodox church in Ukraine, formed at a unity council in Kyiv on 15 December 2018 and granted independence, called autocephaly, by the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople on 6 January 2019. Its first head is Metropolitan Epiphanius.

Ukraine's Orthodox Christians trace their faith to the baptism of Kievan Rus' in 988. For centuries most of them belonged to the Russian Orthodox Church, run from Moscow. After Russia seized Crimea and backed war in the east in 2014, the demand for a church free of Moscow grew strong.

Moscow called the move illegal and broke communion with Constantinople, a deep split in the Orthodox world. Many parishes have since moved to the new church, more so after Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022. In 2023 it began holding services in the Kyiv Pechersk Lavra, the country's most famous monastery.
